title: One extra letter shifts the groups
hook: Predict the result, then reveal the sequence.

knows: DNA and RNA are sequences of chemical building blocks.
doesNotKnow: Inserting one base gives AUGAGAACCA. Reading from the same start produces AUG | AGA | ACC, with one trailing base; the reading frame after the insertion has shifted.

misconception: The original sequence and the resulting sequence must have the same interpretation.
objective: Inserting one base gives AUGAGAACCA. Reading from the same start produces AUG | AGA | ACC, with one trailing base; the reading frame after the insertion has shifted.

claims.text: Question, answer, diagram and explanation: A message is read AUG | GAA | CCA. Insert A immediately after AUG. How are the next complete triplets grouped? Inserting one base gives AUGAGAACCA. Reading from the same start produces AUG | AGA | ACC, with one trailing base; the reading frame after the insertion has shifted.

Recall: A single nucleotide is inserted into a coding region. What can happen to the downstream reading frame? An insertion of one nucleotide shifts downstream triplet grouping when the same reading start is used.
The figure is a simplified model and is not to scale.
